Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations.  

Sarah Johnson:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Consumer Brands Inc.'s third quarter results. With me on the call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Ramirez, Chief Marketing Officer; Emily Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Innovation Officer; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Thompson.  

Mike Thompson:  
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Global Consumer Brands Inc. delivered a solid third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.  

Our discussion today will cover seven key aspects: our summary of financial results and outlook; organic sales growth rate; decomposition of organic sales growth into volume, price, and mix; pricing actions taken and their impact on sales; market share trends by category and region; capital expenditure plans and priorities; and organic sales growth guidance for next quarter and the full year.  

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.  

Lisa Chen:  
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $14.2 billion, representing a 3.2% increase compared to the prior year. This included 5.2% organic sales growth, which outperformed peers like Procter & Gamble and Unilever reporting mid-single-digit gains amid ongoing inflation pressures. Gross margin expanded 210 basis points to 42.3%, driven by supply chain productivity, moderating input costs in commodities such as cocoa down 10% quarter-over-quarter, and favorable pricing realization. Operating income reached $2.1 billion, while diluted earnings per share came in at $1.42, up 8.7% adjusted. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.  

Let me provide a more comprehensive summary of our financial results and outlook. Our third quarter performance highlights resilience in a tough macroeconomic setting, with persistent inflation, supply chain challenges, and shifting consumer behaviors. Net sales of $14.2 billion rose 3.2% year-over-year, our ninth straight quarter of growth. Organic sales advanced 2.8% overall, blending 1.1% volume/mix and 1.7% net pricing, beating the CPG industry average of 1.5% per NielsenIQ. Unfavorable FX, mainly a stronger dollar versus the Brazilian real and Indian rupee, shaved 1.5%.  

By segment, Household & Personal Care grew 4.1% organically on pricing to counter surfactant and packaging inflation, now eased to 8% from 15%. Volumes were flat with North American share gains via promotions. Beauty & Grooming accelerated to 5.2%, powered by prestige skincare double-digit volumes and e-commerce at 28% of sales, up from 22%, amid wellness trends. Nutrition & Snacks achieved 1.9% organic growth despite private label pressure, offset by low-sugar plant-based innovations akin to KIND bars.  

Adjusted EPS of $1.42 beat guidance, up 8.7% adjusted or 11.2% core excluding FX. Gross margins hit 53.4% in some metrics, our best in five quarters, thanks to the $500 million Supply Chain 2.0 program using SAP and Palantir AI for 12% inventory reduction to 65 days. Operating margins rose 140 basis points to 22.1% with SG&A leverage to 28.5%. Free cash flow was $2.1 billion, up 15%, funding $1.2 billion buybacks and a 7% dividend hike to $0.78. Net leverage at 2.1x supports M&A, like our $1.8 billion European clean beauty deal.  

Regionally, North America at 45% of sales grew 4.5% organically, gaining 60 bps share to 14.2% per Circana via hero pricing on multipacks. Europe/MEA at 35% managed 2.1% amid energy costs, with UK laundry strength and 25% recycled packaging ahead of schedule. Asia-Pacific/LATAM at 20% posted 1.8%, with APAC noodles strong but LatAm pricing cautious on hyperinflation; $200 million local production hedges FX.  

For full-year 2023, we're raising guidance: organic sales 3.0-3.5% from 2.5-3.0%, adjusted EPS growth 9-10%, gross margins up 100-150 bps to 53%. FCF conversion 95%+. Our CPG Evolution includes $1 billion digital over three years, doubling DTC to 10% by 2025 via Shopify. Pipeline has 50+ health launches for the $500 billion functional food market at 8% CAGR. Portfolio shaping eyes $2-3 billion divestitures for pet nutrition adjacencies. Scope 3 emissions down 12% via Brazilian soy partnerships.  

Turning to our organic sales growth rate, it reached 5.4% for the quarter, beating our 4-5% midpoint and accelerating for five quarters. Year-to-date at 6.1%, on pace for 5.5-6.5% full-year. This pure measure excludes M&A and FX, blending 1.8% volume and 3.6% net price-mix. We gained 40 bps share per IRI/Nielsen, with household penetration up for EverClean laundry and VitaGlow vitamins.  

Pricing/mix led with 4.2% average increases in three waves to offset 7-9% COGS inflation in palm oil, PET, and hypochlorite. Value tiers like BudgetGuard saw only 2.8% to hold velocity. Mix added 0.6 points via premiumization, EarthPure sustainable cleaners up 18% versus Unilever's Domestos. Volume at 1.8% topped P&G's 1.1% and Colgate's 0.9%, from 1.2 ACV points in NA and 12 new items like NutriBoost bars at 25% trial in Walmart/Kroger.  

North America delivered 7.2% organic with 2.1% volume, club channels +12%, e-comm 22%. Europe 2.8% with -1.2% volume but NPM 4.0%, carbon-neutral VitaGlow +15% in Scandinavia. APAC/LATAM 9.6%, APAC volumes 4.5% in Indonesia/India, LatAm NPM 6.2% hedged.  

Strategic drivers: $250 million divestiture proceeds into functional beverages like HydraSpark; 40% NA localization cutting freight; Salesforce CDP boosting DTC 35%; 60% How2Recycle certified for Gen Z uplift. Q4 guidance 5-7% organic, volume to 2.5% on holidays.  

On decomposition, organic growth was 5.2%, with volume 2.1% improving from Q2's 1.4%. NA led at 3.2% via FreshGlow and ZestBurst velocity, 110 bps laundry share on CleanBoost enzymes, 98% ACV. EMEA flat on snacks downtrading, but AquaPure +8%. LATAM 4.5% on Family Value packs, APAC -1.2% offset by India rural expansion.  

Price contributed 2.4% with 3-4% list hikes on 70% portfolio as inflation eased to 2.8%. NA +3.8%, EMEA +2.9% with 85% base integrity, EM +4.2% rolled back selectively. Mix 0.7 points strongest in years, shifting to health/wellness +12% share, GreenVital plant-milk +25% volume at premium ASPs, e-comm 18% skewing premium, snacks HealthCrunch +300 bps.  

Tailwinds: 22 new premium SKUs, S&OP stockouts to 2.3%, quick-commerce 22% incremental volume. Q4: 4-6% organic, volume 2.5%, price 1.5-2%, mix 0.8%.  

Regarding pricing actions, they drove 6.2% to organic NRG, total 4.1% with -2.1% volume. YTD 6.8%, gross margins +210 bps. Selective 5-8% hikes: Snacks 7.2% on NutriCrunch/ZestChip for 15% cocoa spike, promo depth 18% vs. category 22%, AI engine +12% realization. Snacks NRG +5.3%, mix +1.8% premium Vitality +15%.  

US 7.1% in Beverages AquaPure/Energize for PET, volume flat beating category. Europe 5.4% tempered, Health volumes +2.1%. EM 8.3%, India ZestChip Mini +12%. Elasticity -1.8 improving, 150 bps NA snacks share. Q4 4-6% pricing, 20 premium SKUs. Trade spend 22.4%.  

Market share trends show 120 bps dollar gain overall, 11th straight quarter, outpacing 2.1% category growth. IRI/Nielsen tracked.  

Snacks (35% revenue): +180 bps to 14.2% global, #2 to Frito-Lay. NA 18.5% +210 bps on NutriTrail 40% less sugar, 92% ACV, velocity 112. Europe 11.8% +140 bps eco-packaging. APAC/LATAM 9.5% +90 bps, China Tmall +25%, Brazil flavors.  

Beverages (25%): +150 bps to 12.8%, VitaQuench +8.4% vs. +3.2%. NA 16.1% +190 bps, 95% ACV convenience. Europe 10.2% +80 bps. EM 8.7% +220 bps, India pouches 6.5%, Mexico 11.3%.  

Personal Care (25%): +90 bps to 13.5%. NA 17.2% +110 bps PureGlow DTC Amazon 25%. Europe 12.1% +50 bps clean beauty. APAC/LATAM 9.8% +130 bps Indonesia sachets, Brazil 11.5%.  

Levers: 15% R&D high-growth like pea-protein, 2,500 distribution points ghost kitchens/TikTok, ACV 94%, premium ASP +4.2% NA/Europe, local sourcing EM, 65% FSC-certified. FY24 100-150 bps gains, $200M ASEAN capex.  

On capital expenditure, FY2024 guidance $1.25 billion, +12% from $1.12 billion FY2023, 4.2% of sales below historical 5-6%. 45% or $560 million maintenance for 120 facilities, filling lines VitalEats, PureSpring bottling, downtime <2%.  

55% $690 million growth/transformation. Supply chain $350 million: NA $120 million Greenfield Indiana robotics +25% FreshGlow, Asia $105 million Vietnam greenfield $80 million low-moisture snacks SE Asia $15B market 12% CAGR, H2 2025 output 3.5-year payback 18-20% ROIC. Europe $75 million Dutch PureSpring debottlenecking EU Green Deal, 9% premium hydration.  

Digital/Industry 4.0 $200 million: $90 million AI Siemens sensors -15% energy Ohio pilot, Scope 1/2 -25% by 2030. $60 million e-comm micro-fulfillment US/UK PepsiCo-style, e-comm 22% sales, DTC +30% GlowEssence.  

Sustainability/innovation $140 million: $70 million circular PET PureSpring 50% recycled by 2026 ahead Nestlé, millennial 68% Kantar preference. $50 million R&D precision fermentation nutritionals alt-protein $8B 14% CAGR.  

Sequenced for 10-12% IRR short-term, 20%+ long. Funded organically, 2.8x debt/EBITDA, 60% FCF returns, 2.4% yield. NA 3.5% intensity, Europe 5%, EM 6.5% for 15% growth. Premium SKUs 45%, outpace IRI flat 2-3% volumes. Underpins 8-10% FY2024 EPS growth.  

Finally, outlook: Q4 organic 4-6%, 1-2% pricing, 2-4% volume/mix. Snacks low-single NutriBars relaunch 5,000 Walmart/Kroger doors, Amazon +15%. Beverages mid-single zero-sugar vs. Monster. NA 5-7% value multipacks premium beauty. Europe 3-5% +4% pricing sustainable PET +8% loyalty. EM 4-6% sachets double-digit. FX -50 bps headwind, AI SAP IBP forecast error 8%, dual-source 80% cocoa/palm.  

FY2025 raised to 5-7% organic, $28.5-29.0B sales, 3% pricing 2-4% volume/mix H2 acceleration: 12 SKUs keto microbiome, +2% ACV dollar stores DTC 8%, affordable premium 70% better-for-you. $200M Project Horizon savings 100 bps margins 42-43%. Risks tariffs Red Sea, 95% on-time delivery.  

Following my remarks, David will provide an update on our marketing and brand performance.  

David Ramirez:  
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to see strong performance across our key brands. Our marketing investments are driving increased consumer engagement, and we are particularly pleased with the results of our recent GlowUp campaign, which boosted e-commerce velocity by 15% and reinforced premiumization in skincare and snacks, aligning with our AI-driven personalization efforts that have improved engagement through tailored bundles and omnichannel strategies.  

After me, Emily will discuss our supply chain initiatives.  

Emily Patel:  
Thank you, David. Our focus remains on optimizing our supply chain to enhance efficiency and resilience. We are implementing advanced analytics to improve forecasting and inventory management, including the AI predictive maintenance and localization efforts that reduced stockouts and energy use, while advancing circular packaging to cut waste and meet sustainability goals ahead of peers.  

Finally, Raj will share insights on our innovation pipeline.  

Raj Singh:  
Thank you, Emily. We are excited about the progress we are making on our new product development initiatives. Our pipeline is robust, and we are confident that our innovations will drive future growth. Our recent product, VitalEats Pro Bar, is showing promising early results with 25% trial rates, 20% more protein, and strong share gains in health snacking, contributing to volume lifts and positioning us in the $15 billion category growing at 7% CAGR.  

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.  

Operator:  
Thank you. If you would like to register a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.  

John Smith:  
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce packaging waste and the associated cost savings?  

Emily Patel:  
Thanks for the question, John. We're making significant strides in packaging waste reduction as part of our sustainability capex, allocating $70 million to circular lines like recycled PET blow-molding for PureSpring, targeting 50% recycled content by 2026 ahead of Nestlé. This has driven cost savings through efficiency and resonates with consumers, where 68% of millennials prioritize eco-packaging per Kantar, while supporting margin protection and regulatory compliance like the EU Packaging Directive. Early pilots show 15% energy reductions and improved ROIC.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan.  

Maria Lopez:  
How are you leveraging data analytics to personalize your marketing efforts and improve customer engagement?  

David Ramirez:  
Great question, Maria. We're heavily investing in data analytics, including our AI-driven personalization engine on Salesforce CDP and partnerships with NielsenIQ for real-time elasticity, boosting DTC sales 35% via tailored bundles on our app and platforms like Instacart. This has lifted omnichannel to 45% penetration, e-commerce to 22%, and loyalty scores +8% in Europe, while dynamic promo adjustments improve price realization by 12% and engagement in high-growth channels like TikTok Shop.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Alex Kim with Morgan Stanley.  

Alex Kim:  
What is the expected impact of recent commodity price increases on your gross margins?  

Lisa Chen:  
Alex, thanks. Recent commodity spikes like 15% YoY cocoa and palm oil have been offset by our pricing discipline at 6.2% contribution, hedging 85% of 2024 needs, and productivity from Supply Chain 2.0, delivering 210 bps gross margin expansion to 42.3-53.4%. We expect moderation to 2-3% inflation, with Q4 pricing 4-6% and $200 million savings funding further 100 bps expansion to 42-43%, maintaining resilience versus peers.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Barclays.  

Sarah Lee:  
Can you discuss the competitive landscape and any emerging trends that are impacting your market share?  

Mike Thompson:  
Sarah, appreciate it. The landscape is intense with P&G, Unilever, PepsiCo, but we've gained 120 bps overall, 11th straight quarter, through precision innovation like plant-based extensions, distribution mastery adding 2,500 points in ghost kitchens and TikTok, and regional tailoring—premium in NA/Europe, value in EM. Trends like premiumization, health adjacencies, sustainability (Scope 3 -18%, 65% FSC), and GLP-1 pivots to portionable packs position us for 100-150 bps FY24 gains, outpacing flat category volumes.  

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.  

Mike Thompson:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your thoughtful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to updating you next quarter.  

Sarah Johnson:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
